'Tis the Season to Give Back!

Dear Columbus Recreation and Parks Supporter, 

Just a friendly reminder that this is the final week to support our Holiday Adopt a Center program! Staff are finishing up final purchases, volunteers are wrapping gifts and the 26 community centers are decorating in anticipation of their holiday parties to bring cheer to Columbus families!

If you have already supported our Holiday Adopt a Center program--THANK YOU! If you haven’t yet made a gift and are interested in supporting Columbus families for the holidays this year, we would love to have your support. Thank you, and happy holidays!

Erika Shemberg

item.title: Giving Back This Holiday Season
item.description:
Giving Back This Holiday Season

Dear Columbus Recreation and Parks Supporter, 

The holidays are upon us! Columbus Recreation and Parks is gearing up to spread holiday joy to families through our Adopt a Center program! Thousands of meals, warm winter items and gifts will be distributed over the next few weeks to people who need a little extra help this holiday season. As prices on food and other necessities continue to rise, our community needs your help now more than ever.

If you are able, please consider making a contribution to our Holiday Adopt a Center efforts. Thank you for your support and investment in local Columbus families to make the holidays brighter for them!

Thank you, and happy holidays!

Erika Shemberg
Development Manager

item.title: Grateful and Thankful This Thanksgiving
item.description:
Much To Be Thankful For

Dear Columbus Recreation and Parks Supporter,

Thanksgiving is right around the corner! As we think about what we are thankful for as we approach this holiday season, we wanted to reach out to you about our Holiday Adopt a Center program. This holiday program provides hot meals to almost 6,000 Columbus families; provides winter hats, gloves and coats to kids; and brings the joy of holiday gifts to kids right here in your community. All meals and gifts are distributed through 25 of our Columbus Recreation and Parks Department’s community centers between mid-November and late December.

We cannot help thousands of people each year without your support. Please consider making a donation or going to the Amazon wish list and purchasing a gift. Thank you for investing in Adopt a Center—reaching out to thousands of Columbus families would not be possible without you!

Thank you,

Erika Shemberg
Development Manager

item.title: Make the Holidays Brighter
item.description:
Make the Holidays Brighter

Dear Columbus Recreation and Parks Supporter,

As the weather is getting chillier and fall is settling in, we are beginning to prepare for the holiday season! We think about all the underserved populations and families living in the neighborhoods where our community centers are located. Columbus Recreation and Parks operates 28 community centers; all but four are located in ZIP codes with a poverty rate of 20 percent or higher. With an inflation rate of over 8 percent, we know people are going to be struggling to provide holiday food and gifts for their families.

Columbus Recreation and Parks Department operates the Holiday Adopt a Center program to help provide hot, nutritious meals, warm winter items and gifts to adults and children. The success of the program is thanks to generous companies, organizations and individuals who support the program by making a financial donation or purchasing gifts on the Amazon wish list. I hope you will consider helping us this year. Learn more.

Thank you,

Erika Shemberg
Development Manager

item.title: Please Welcome the New Community Relations Chief
item.description:
Please Welcome the New Community Relations Chief

Dear Columbus Recreation and Parks Supporter,

We wanted to share that Dominque Shank joined our department on May 2 as our new Community Relations Chief. In this role, she will lead the Customer Service, Development and Communications functions. As a valuable supporter of the department, it's important you know who is leading this great team. 

Dominique brings to the department nearly 20 years of experience in marketing, development and customer service. She has a breadth of experience including running her own marketing strategy business, serving as the development officer for the Columbus Urban League and serving as director of marketing communications, community relations with Beacon 360 Management. 

She earned a bachelor's and master's degree in business administration-marketing/ marketing management from Xavier University and a master's degree in public administration from the University of Texas at Dallas. 

The Community Relations team looks forward to working with Dominique to make an even bigger positive impact in this community.

Making it Easier to See What’s Available
at YOUR Recreation and Parks Department

To make it easier for you to see what’s coming up at your Columbus Recreation and Parks Department, some exciting changes are coming to this newsletter!

Beginning in November, you’ll receive the newsletter every Thursday evening so you can plan for the coming week – don’t worry, we’re making the newsletter shorter so it will be easy to skim and pull out what’s important to you.

As you read the new format, tell us what you think! Send your feedback to ColumbusRecParks@Columbus.gov.

Rallying to Keep Our Parks Clean

Monday, Columbus Recreation and Parks partnered with Columbus Crew and Ohio Blind Soccer for a litter cleanup at Rhodes Park. Volunteers and staff from all three organizations spend two hours picking up litter. This was a great way to work with volunteers and community partners to keep our parks beautiful!

With the increased traffic in parks, preventing litter is a year-round effort that will take all of us. Here are some easy ways you can prevent litter:

  1. Set a good example. Always throw trash and recycling in a proper receptacle.
  2. Take your trash with you. With the increased in park visitors, trash cans are filling up quickly. Keep a litter bag in your car and hang on to litter until you find a trash can.
  3. Encourage others to not litter. Remind others about the proper way to dispose or trash and recycling, and report littering.

New Center Managers Here to Serve the Community 

Community centers serve a critical role in neighborhoods across the City, connecting you with activities, resources - and each other!

With some recent retirements, five centers have new managers. Some are familiar faces while others are new to the center, or the department.  

  • Blackburn – Kevin Dulaney
  • Howard – Renny Tyson
  • Scioto Southland – Bobby Shaun Ballard
  • Westgate – Malcolm Wilkes
  • Whetstone – Jeff Sheppard

Center managers are charged with serving you and keeping the center running. If you have questions or feedback, please reach out to your local center manager. 

Making Fitness Fun: Kids’ Run

Join us Oct. 23 at 10 a.m. for the 2021 Kids’ Run!

This year’s theme is Superheroes, so wear your favorite costume and come check out this family-friendly event! We will have distances for each age group, starting with a Toddler/Diaper Dash. All registered participants will receive a medal for participation. Participating locations are:

  • Linden Community Center (1350 Briarwood Ave, 43211)
  • Scioto Southland Community Center (3901 Parsons Ave, 43207)
  • Westgate Community Center (455 S Westgate Ave, 43204)
  • Far East Community Center (1826 Lattimer Dr, 43227)

Online registration is only $2; there are no other costs to participate. Register online or at your local community center.

Get Spooked by the Dracula Radio Play

Get ready to be frightened by our Grandview Carriage Place Players’ newest performance: Dracula. This radio play will be released every Wednesday in October, starting Oct. 13.

Get into the spirit and check out this scary entertainment for preteens through adults!

For more information, visit the Theatre page.

Help Shape the New West Case Road Park

Columbus Recreation and Parks is developing a new 58-acre park at the historic sheep farm located at 2425 West Case Road. The site will become one of the major greenspaces in northwest Columbus and has a wide range of possibilities—from sports to hiking to nature to special programming—all within a short walk of more than 6,000 residents. 

To ensure the new park meets the needs of residents, we want your input! Complete this brief survey to tell us what you want to see. If you haven’t been to the site, join us Oct. 16 for a walking tour and envision what’s possible!

Learn more about the project, and sign up to receive email updates!

Make a Difference in Your Community This Holiday Season

 If you, your family, business or organization is looking for a way to give back this holiday season, please consider our Adopt a Center program. It’s convenient, easy and makes a difference.

The Adopt a Center program provides gifts and meals that are distributed through an event at community centers. Last year, 6,300 meals were served, and more than 2,800 children received gifts, thanks to the generosity of nearly 600 individuals and 30 organizations/businesses.

Anyone can participate–even a $5 contribution makes a difference!

Make a difference in your community this holiday season. Visit crpfoundation.org/adoptacenter to learn more, make a donation or purchase a gift.

Celebrate, Learn About Nature’s Dynamos at Pollinator Field Day

Pollinators–such as birds, bees and butterflies–are important to our environment and world. They pollinate trees, flowers and crops; plants that provide our food and food and shelter for other animals. Did you know that pollinators are responsible for one out of every three bites of food?

Celebrate nature’s dynamos at free Pollinator Field Days in September and October! There’s something for all ages, including kids’ activities, a pollinator habitat scavenger hunt and a butterfly catch-and-release–we’ll learn how to tag monarchs if we catch any. We’ll try out the free iNaturalist app to identify and document the flowers and pollinator species we see. You can also volunteer to help with habitat restoration efforts. Events are outdoors and COVID-19 safety protocols will be followed. Walk-ins are welcome–register online to volunteer. It’s sure to be a day of fun and learning!

  • Sept. 18, 10 a.m.-12 p.m. at McKnight Outdoor Recreation Center, 3228 Indian Village Road. Learn more.
  • Oct. 9, from 10 a.m.-1 p.m. at Whetstone Park Prairie, 3901 North High Street. Learn more; register to voulunteer.

“Fall” into Wellness at the Senior Wellness Jamboree

The Senior Wellness Jamboree is happening in person this year! The FREE event takes place Oct. 1, 9 a.m.-2 p.m. at the Franklin Park Adventure Center, 1755 E. Broad Street.

Join us for a fun fitness walk that offers distances for every fitness level. Participate in demo classes and activities, get tips and resources for a healthy lifestyle and win prizes. Lunch and refreshments will be provided, sponsored by Dedicated Senior Medical.

Brought to you by Columbus Recreation and Parks and Franklin County Office on Aging.

Learn more and register. Contact Katie Teggart at 614-645-3331 with questions.

Explore Columbus Art

The Cultural Arts Center (CAC) is a stop in the Greater Columbus Arts Council’s (GCAC) Columbus Makes Art Art Makes Columbus Passport program.  CAC is one of many stops where you can get "stamped" with a sticker in your very own GCAC passport. Earn prizes as you fill up your passport. Passports are available at the Center if you're just getting started. 

Learn more about the Columbus Makes Art Passport program.

Double Your Impact: Donate to PLAY Today

The Brian S. Casey Family Memorial Fund is matching all gifts to PLAY Scholarship Fund. The fund was established to honor Brian and his 19-year-old daughter, Megan, who tragically lost their lives in a plane crash in 2016. Brian was a strong believer in the PLAY program and served on the PLAY Golf Committee for many years. His wife, Sharon, started the fund to continue Brian’s commitment to the PLAY program.

Thanks to the generosity of the Casey Family, every dollar donated to the PLAY program will be matched (up to $10,000). Please double your impact by making a donation today. 

Free Leadership Development Program for 6-8th Graders

Do you have a middle schooler who is a future leader for our great city? Have them apply to City Leaders today!

The City Leaders program develops the leaders of tomorrow so our children stay here and serve as the future leaders of Columbus. Participants meet monthly to engage in hands-on learning opportunities, meetings and mentoring by city leadership. They explore topics such as science, technology, arts, history, education, health and nutrition, social services, law enforcement, safety, government, economic development and community service. The experience improves students’ public speaking skills, facilitation skills, teamwork, community awareness and overall leadership attitude. This free opportunity is open to City of Columbus middle schoolers (grades 6-8 and ages 10-15). 

Apply today! Applications are due Sept. 30.

Partnering to Conserve Our Environment 

Parks serve an essential role in improving the quality of life for residents. Parks benefit our residents and community by providing a place for residents of all ages and abilities to connect with nature, which benefits our mental and physical health; protecting our environment by cleaning the air and water, replenishing aquifers, reducing stormwater runoff and safeguarding wildlife habitat; and strengthening our economic well‐being by conserving energy and resources

Columbus Recreation and Parks works to conserve and protect our parks, greenspaces, trees and wildlife. In addition to maintaining 19 nature preserves and 33 pollinator gardens, last year we removed 94,000 bags of trash from parks, spread 35 pounds of prairie seed and planted nearly 1,000 trees.

Be an advocate for your parks and environment-join our conservation efforts!

In April, we launched a volunteer conservation program focused on pollinator planting, invasive removal, litter cleanup and stream restoration. This season, volunteers have assisted with a creek cleanup at Holton Park, honeysuckle removal and litter cleanup at Academy and Wolfe Park, prairie maintenance at Whetstone and much more.

If you’re interested in joining us for an upcoming conservation project, sign up online, or contact Betty Blockinger, volunteer services manager, at BKBlockinger@columbus.gov.

Stay Engaged and Active This Fall: Register for Activities

The end of summer doesn’t have to mean the end of fun! Columbus Recreation and Parks offers activities for all ages and interests throughout the year. From arts and crafts to fitness, sports and senior activities, there’s something for everyone.

We’re gearing up for fall programming, and registration opens in just a few short weeks for the following activities:

  • Creative arts classes: Activities offered by the Cultural Arts Center (CAC) begin Sept. 7. Registration opens Aug. 28 at 8:30 a.m.; register online or in person at 139 E. Main St., 43215.
  • Swim lessons, water fitness and more: Activities at the Columbus Aquatics Center begin Sept. 20. Registration opens Sept. 7 at 9 a.m.; register online or in person at the Columbus Aquatics Center, 1160 Hunter Ave., 43201.
  • Community center-based, adaptive sports and outdoor recreation activities: Activities for 50+ begin Sept. 13; all other activities begin Sept. 14. Registration for all other activities begins Sept. 7 at 12:30 p.m.; register online or in person at your neighborhood community center.
  • Sports leagues and tournaments: Play goes well into the fall! Explore options and register online.

Keep the fun going and engage with your community this fall with Columbus Recreation and Parks programming! Browse the many options available and sign up.

Columbus Symphony Brings Free Concerts to Parks

Whether you’re a long-time fan of the symphony or have been meaning to experience your first performance, Columbus Symphony (CSO) and Columbus Recreation and Parks have a great opportunity for you!

This month, the CSO is partnering with Columbus Recreation and Parks to bring free concerts to parks across the city. These “Columbus Symphony Community Concerts” are 45-minute, live orchestra performances that feature a mix of symphonic and pops music, including pieces from Elgar, Sousa, and Tchaikovsky as well as “Highlights from The Lion King,” “Best of the Beatles,” “Michael Jackson Hit Mix” and more. Concerts include:

  • Aug. 18, 6:30 p.m. – Driving Park*
  • Aug. 19, 6:30 p.m. – Marion Franklin Park
  • Aug. 20, 6:30 p.m. – Dodge Park*
  • Aug. 21, 6:30 p.m. – Mayme Moore Park*

*A small ensemble of Urban Strings’ youth orchestra will perform a 'pre-concert' from 6-6:20 p.m.

Admission is free! Bring your blankets and chairs and pack a picnic. See you at the symphony! The show will go on rain or shine! 

Photo credit: Stephen Pariser

Get a Head Start on Your Plans for Holiday Giving

While summer isn’t officially over, Columbus Recreation and Parks is gearing up for the holidays!

Many residents still are facing financial difficulties made worse by the pandemic. And, with cases on COVID-19 on the rise and the spread of the Delta variant, there are likely to be more families in need this holiday season.

For the second year, the department will partner with generous groups, organizations, business and individuals to make the holiday season brighter for those in need through the Adopt a Center program. Sponsors ‘adopt’ a community center and provide gifts and meals that are distributed at a group meal, holiday party or other community event. Last year, 6,300 meals were served and more than 2,800 children received gifts, thanks to the generosity of nearly 600 individuals and 30 organizations/businesses.

There are opportunities for individuals, work teams, organizations and companies to participate, no matter your budget:

  • Make a financial donation: Donations will be used to purchase toys, food and other needed items for children and families.
  • Purchase an item for a family or child in need: Visit our Amazon Wish List and purchase an item for a family in need. Items will be delivered directly to the City of Columbus for distribution.
  • Adopt a community center: If your company or organization can help in a big way, we are looking for sponsors to provide financial or in-kind donations to fill a wide variety of needs for the community surrounding the center. 

To learn more, visit crpfoundation.org/adoptacenter or contact Erika Shemberg at EJshemberg@columbus.gov.

Fresh and Exciting Changes Coming to Many Playgrounds 

This is a big year for our playgrounds!

Many playgrounds across the city are getting updates in 2021. Improvements vary by park and could include upgrading some of the equipment and adding rubberized surfaces. Some playgrounds will be completely replaced and could include new features. We're also adding universally accessible playgrounds and features in some parks so kids of all physical abilities can play. 

If you see work being done on a playground in your local park, watch for a fresh and exciting things to come!

Celebrating How Parks, Recreation Make Our Community Great

July is National Park and Recreation Month. This annual event, hosted by the National Recreation and Park Association, celebrates the positive impact recreation and parks departments have on communities across the country.

This year's theme, Our Park and Recreation Story, celebrates the history of departments. And at 111 years old, Columbus Recreation and Parks has quite a rich history! Did you know: 

  • Established on July 15, 1910, the City Recreation Department enriched Columbus by finding ways to make streets, alleys, boulevards, parks and public grounds more beautiful. On Jan. 2, 1972, the City Recreation Department merged with the Division of Forestry and Parks to become the Columbus Recreation and Parks Department.
  • The City features two skate parks. Dodge Skate Park, our first skate park, is 16 acres and features three all-concrete bowls; 3, 4, and 6 feet deep. The 4-foot bowl can function as a half-pipe, while the 6-foot bowl has an intense "verte." The park was designed by Frank Hawk, legendary skateboarder Tony Hawk’s father.
  • You can enjoy the outdoors at more than 400 parks across the City. One, English Park (also known as the Children's Africentric Playground), is home to the Kwanzaa Playground. The park focuses on positive African-American images based around the concept that "it takes a whole village to raise a child." The park was renovated in 2014 with new play equipment and art restoration as well as a new portal by artist Queen Brooks. Learn more about our parks.
  • Residents from preschool to age 99+ can access programs catering to a variety of interests including the arts, fitness and educational pursuits. Many are low- or no-cost, and all are designed to help residents connect with nature, wellness and creativity-and each other! One program, City Leaders, is celebrating its 10th anniversary, and introduces middle school students to the leaders and locations that make Columbus great. It educates middle school youth to become model citizens and future leaders of our City. Explore all current recreational opportunities.

You, our residents, are what brings our story to life! We want to hear how you have engaged with us over the years. Share your photos and memories on social media by using the hashtag #OurParkAndRecStory and tagging us.

Help Keep our Parks Beautiful

Columbus is home to more than 400 parks, where residents can work out, relax and engage with nature year-round. During the pandemic, our parks have been a place for residents to safely get outside and spend time with family and friends, and traffic in parks has significantly increased.

Unfortunately, littering also has increased in our parks.

Littering sometimes is unintentional, such as when something falls out of your bag without you knowing. But most littering is done intentionally, often because people are lazy or careless, don’t want to wait to find a trash can or see other litter and follow suit.

A study by Keep America Beautiful found the most littered items include cigarette butts, food wrappers, plastic bottles, disposable cups, grocery bags, straws, beverage cans, and tire and vehicle debris.

Preventing litter isn’t just about keeping our parks beautiful, it’s about protecting our health and the environment. Here’s how litter affects our world:

  • Litter causes pollution as it degrades and releases chemicals and microparticles. For example, cigarette butts can contain chemicals such as arsenic and formaldehyde that make their way into the soil and water.
  • Litter can kill wildlife. Researchers estimate that over 1 million animals die each year after ingesting or becoming entrapped in litter.
  • Litter facilitates the spread of disease. Litter is a breeding ground for bacteria and diseases, and can spread diseases, viruses and parasites. 

YOU can help prevent litter! Here are some easy ways:

  1. Set a good example. Always throw trash and recycling in a proper receptacle.
  2. Take your trash with you. With the increased traffic in parks, trash cans are filling up quickly. Keep a litter bag in your car and hang on to litter until you find a trash can.
  3. Encourage others to not litter. Remind others about the proper way to dispose or trash and recycling, and report littering.
  4. Volunteer to clean up a park. Sign up for a volunteer shift to clean up and beautify your favorite park. Learn more about our volunteer program.

Our parks enhance the quality of life for all of our residents. Please, help keep our parks beautiful!

Live Theatre Returns with Shakespeare

Theatre is BACK!

Columbus Recreation and Parks is setting the stage for a terrific weekend of Shakespeare! Join us for “A Midsummer Night’s Dream,” presented by Grandview Carriage Place Players. This comedy about star-crossed lovers, incompetent actors and the magical fairies who create havoc for them all as they wander through the woods will be a night of laughs for the whole family.

7 p.m. July 29, 30 and 31
McKinley Shelter House
1661 Goodale Blvd., Grandview Heights

Tickets are FREE! Be sure to bring lawn chairs and blankets.

For more information, visit columbus.gov/Theatre or contact John Heisel at 614-645-3715 or Marta Durban at 614-488-3111.

Last Chance: Share What YOU Want to See in the New Columbus Community Sports Park

The deadline to share your feedback and help shape the new Columbus Community Sports Park has been extended to July 30.

The new sports park will be a new, centrally-located park and recreation space located on the grounds of the historic Crew Stadium and adjacent to the Ohio State Fairgrounds along Interstate 71, between East 17th Avenue and Hudson Street. It will benefit nearby neighborhoods, providing much-needed access to park and recreation space to the 200,000 residents who live within 3 miles of the site. It will also benefit the City and region as a destination for tournaments, leagues and events. Learn more about this exciting new facility by watching this short video!

The City is asking for feedback on the activities and facilities that residents would like to have at the new Columbus Community Sports Park. Take the survey and give your input today.

Learn more and sign up for project updates at CRPDSports.org/CommunitySportsPark.

Improvements Enhance Rental Venues at North Bank, Goodale

Did you know you can rent space for family gatherings, corporate events, weddings and more at Columbus Recreation and Parks facilities spread throughout Columbus? Recent renovations at North Bank Park Pavilion and Goodale Shelterhouse enhance the experience for you and your guests. 

At North Bank, a new covering extends over the existing patio and increases the capacity from 100 people to 200, allowing for larger groups without needing to rent a tent. This permanent covering also will serve as a shaded area for the public when this facility along the Scioto Mile is not being rented. Other renovations include a small dressing room for weddings and a kitchen modification to make it more caterer-friendly. When you walk along the Scioto Mile, make sure to check out this improvement!

Goodale Shelterhouse, a popular rental facility at Goodale Park, recently underwent a major facelift. Improvements include a completely updated kitchen and bathrooms. The event space also was updated with new doors, windows, flooring, lighting and adding a hardwood ceiling.

Learn more about all Columbus Recreation and Parks rental sites.

item.title: Feeding the Community, DO NOT Feed the Wildlife and Help Shape Your Future Parks and Pools
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Helping Families Access Nutritious Food

Access to adequate, healthy food is key to the overall health and development of children, and to helping families achieve their best. Columbus Recreation and Parks Department's Food Office continues to help residents access free meals and fresh produce. 

According to Feeding America’s most recent data, its 2019 Map the Meal Gap Study, 165,000 Franklin County residents do not have access to sufficient and nutritious foods. This has been made worse by the pandemic, and more families are facing food insecurity for the first time.

The Food Office’s two signature program provides meals and fresh produce to help address this critical need:

  • Go, Lunch!: This Summer Food Program offers free, nutritionally balanced meals during the summer months at community centers along with other various locations. Last summer, more than 472,000 meals were served at over 230 locations in the Columbus area. These meals are served to anyone between the ages of 1–18. Find a location near you.
  • Free Mobile Produce Markets: These markets offer families a week’s worth of free produce. These drive-thru markets are staffed by volunteers wearing masks and gloves who load the produce directly into the trunk or car. Simply drive in, drive up and drive off! Markets are held most Thursdays and Fridays, February through December. See when we are in or close to your neighborhood.

This is a time when many Columbus residents may find themselves in need of additional support. Columbus Recreation and Parks is here to help. If you need assistance, stop by one of the sites. If you know someone who needs assistance, share this information with them.

Visit www.golunch.club to learn more.

“But He Looks Hungry!” Why it’s Best to NOT Feed the Wildlife

Going to the park and feeding the ducks and geese sounds like a lot of fun–and the animals seem to love the tasty treats! But did you know that feeding human food to wildlife is actually harmful and potentially deadly?

This article from the National Park Service explains how feeding wildlife presents several hazards for wildlife, including increasing their chances of being injured and causing health issues that can be fatal. Feeding wildlife human food also increases their scat (waste)!

Please, next time you’re at a park, do not feed the wildlife! You’re making the safe choice for our animal friends.

New Exhibit Features Artists’ Take on Getting Through the Pandemic

Join us June 4–July 10 in the Cultural Arts Center’s Main Gallery for The Art of Surviving a Pandemic. This exhibit features local invited artists who tell their stories about how they continued to work during the COVID-19 pandemic through a variety of art forms including visual, poetry, performance and music. 

Works focus on questions we’ve all been wrestling with–where did their inspirations come from? Did they learn new techniques? Did they have to cope with the loss of loved ones? The exhibit is curated by Leticia Vazquez-Smith, President of the Latino Arts for Humanity.

The Cultural Arts Center galleries are open Mondays 1-4 p.m. and 7-10 p.m., Tuesdays–Thursdays 9 a.m.-4 p.m. and 7-10 p.m., and Fridays-Saturday 9 a.m.-4 p.m.  Register for a visit online or by phone at 614-645-7047.

Help Shape the New Columbus Community Sports Park

As the Columbus Crew prepares to move downtown, our community has a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to shape 25 acres of new green space, park space and recreational programming on the near-northeast side of the City.

The Columbus Community Sports Park will be a new, centrally-located park and recreation space that will benefit nearby neighborhoods, the City and the region. It will provide much-needed access to park and recreation space to the 200,000 residents who live within 3 miles of the site. Facilities, fields and green space will be easily accessible to neighborhoods including: Milo Grogan, Weinland Park, Linden, North Columbus, Glen Echo, Indianola Trace, University District, Clintonville and others.

The Columbus Community Sports Park will be located on the grounds of the historic Crew Stadium and adjacent to the Ohio State Fairgrounds along Interstate 71, between East 17th Avenue and Hudson Street.

The Community Sports Park has two primary components. The first is facilities for organized – formal – sports programs. These will be available for rent by families, local teams, traveling leagues and others. These could include multi-use wood courts, tournament-level synthetic turf fields, indoor field space, meeting rooms, classrooms, a rock climbing wall, a concessions area or covered outdoor pickleball courts.

The second is informal sports and community park spaces, which will be available at no cost to residents and teams. These could include mixed-use grass fields, basketball courts, walking and bicycling trails with exercise stations, green space with an outdoor courtyard or plaza, open shelters, picnic tables, a playground, a splash pad or a skate park.

The City is asking for feedback on the activities and facilities that residents would like to have at the new Columbus Community Sports Park. Take the survey and give your input today: http://bit.ly/ccspsurvey21.

Learn more and sign up for project updates at CRPDSports.org/CommunitySportsPark.

Help Improve Pools and Spray Parks: Attend an Online Public Meeting

Through the Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan, the department is looking for your ideas for potential improvements to all of the aquatics facilities! We have eight outdoor pools, one indoor pool and seven spray parks and fountains. Pre-register for an online public meeting about an aquatics facility close to you! Take the aquatics survey here.

item.title: Summer Fun for the Entire Family, Golden Hobby Reopens, and more
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Summer Fun for the Entire Family

This summer, your family can engage in many fun activities with Columbus Recreation and Parks!

Summer camps: There are still spots in a number of summer camps! Kids ages 6-14 can be active, make new friends and create lifelong memories at a day camp. Camps focus on a variety of activities including arts, fitness, sports, science/STEM, outdoor exploration and adaptive recreation. Learn more and register.

Summer programming: From arts and crafts to fitness and sports, to senior activities, there’s something for everyone in our summer session. Registration for classes and activities with Community Recreation, Seniors/50+ and Get Active Fitness starts at 9:30 a.m. on May 24; programming begins June 7. Learn more and register.

Pools: Pools are back! Pools begin to open Memorial Day Weekend, and all eight pools will be open through the summer. This year, we are waiving admission fees for residents so there’s no cost to attend. However, due to capacity limits, you are asked to register online in advance to ensure a spot. If you need assistance registering, call or stop by your local pool or community center.

Sports Leagues: Kids–and kids at heart–can sign up for a variety of sports leagues including kickball, softball, volleyball, soccer and more. Leagues run throughout the summer and fall. Learn more and register.

Parks and Trails: Did you know that Columbus’ parks offer some unique attractions including 11,000 roses in bloom at Park of Roses, a living recreation of a famous painting at Topiary Park and a nature preserve with a beautiful 35-foot waterfall at Hayden Falls? You can visit a variety of settings without leaving Columbus. How many of the City’s 400 parks can you explore this summer?

Senior Consignment Shop Opens in New Location

Looking for some unique, handmade gifts? Look no further than Golden Hobby Gift Shop!

Golden Hobby Shop will reopen June 1 at its new location in the Columbus Performing Arts Center (CPAC). For 50 years, this senior arts and consignment shop has offered an array of handmade goods for sale, including quilts, ceramics, woodcrafts, paintings and more. All items are made by Columbus-area seniors. The shop is staffed by Columbus Recreation and Parks employees and a group of dedicated senior volunteers.

Located at 549 Franklin Ave. in the downtown Discovery District, the shop’s hours are Tuesday-Saturday, 10 a.m.-4:30 p.m. and Sunday, 1-4 p.m.

Come see what’s new and find a great gift for someone special!

Capital Projects Updates

New Campus to Connect the Community through Creativity

A new Community Creative Campus in Olde Towne East will provide creative programming and wellness activities for all community members. In addition to housing many of the popular programs from the Martin Janis Community Senior Center and Golden Hobby Shop, there is an opportunity to offer new programs and amenities in this space.

You have the opportunity to help shape the new campus. Share what amenities you would like to see within the building and on the surrounding greenspace. Complete a brief online survey by June 3.

Visit www.CbusCreativeCampus.com to learn more and take the survey!

Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan Survey Still Available

There’s still time to share what you need and want to see in Columbus' aquatics facilities and programs! The Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan survey is still open, and so is your opportunity to help shape what Columbus’ pools, spray parks and aquatics programming will look like into the future. Fill out a brief online survey.

Learn more about the Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan by visiting www.ColumbusAquatics.org.

Other updates include:

  • An alternative to close the gap on the Olentangy Trail between Clinton-Como Park and Northmoor Park has been selected. When complete, this project will close the final gap on the trail and enhance connectivity for thousands of walkers, cyclists and runners. Learn more.

New Artist-in-Residence Program Helps Artists Grow While Giving Back

A new Artist-in-Residence program at the Cultural Arts Center (CAC) will foster artists’ development while creating opportunities for CAC and Columbus Recreation and Parks to build a new, diverse network of creative artists in the city.

The artists will have access to studio space at the facility, along with organizational and material support, helping them hone their craft. During their residency, the artists will work with youth at community centers throughout the city, helping aspiring young artists to learn from and be mentored by established professional artists.

The first two artists-in-residence are Tiffany Lawson (pictured left) and Brianna Rhodes. Lawson, the spring/summer resident, is a multidisciplinary artist and Columbus native, who often works with collage, found objects and assemblage. She will serve in residence May 10-Aug. 31. Rhodes, the fall/winter resident, is a dancer, poet and educator from Dayton. She specializes in dance, which she has taught online throughout the pandemic. Her residency runs Sept. 14, 2021-Jan. 4, 2022.

New Date for Champions for PLAY

Due to weather, the 25th Annual Champions for PLAY golf outing was rescheduled for Sept. 24. While everyone was looking forward to the event, the good news is the new date means there’s still room for additional team! Learn more and register.

Contact Erika Shemberg at ejshemberg@columbus.gov or 614-645-1492 with questions.

item.title: Community Centers Open, Caring for Our Trees and Honoring What's Important
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Community Centers Remain Open to Serve Residents

A year into the public health emergency, life is showing some signs of returning to normal. Yet many residents are still feeling the impact to their mental, emotional and financial health.

Columbus Recreation and Parks’ community centers remain open and here to assist residents! The community centers serve as a safe place to engage in a variety of activities including structured programming for all ages and interests, from arts to sports to gaming. Spring session activities (many of which are low- or no-cost) launched this week; explore opportunities and register online. Also, fitness and weight rooms are open to help residents stay active and healthy; sign up through your local community center. These activities not only keep you active and engaged, they serve as an opportunity to connect with your community.

Community center staff also can connect residents in need with critical resources including food and connection to social services. If you’re struggling, we’re here to help–please reach out to a staff member at your local community center.

Give Trees Some Love This Arbor Day!

Let’s hear it for the trees! April 30 is Arbor Day, a day to celebrate trees and the vital role they play in our quality of life. Trees are nature's workhorses, cleaning our air, providing shade and intercepting stormwater. This improves quality of life for all residents.

Each year, Columbus’ trees:

  • Remove 540 pounds of air pollution
  • Remove 18,000 pounds of carbon dioxide, reducing temperatures
  • Absorb 157,000 gallons of stormwater, reducing flooding

Each of us plays a role in protecting our trees. Adding trees to your property helps grow our urban forest; learn how to plant a tree so it thrives! Properly maintaining your trees keeps them healthy over their lifetime; learn how to prune a young tree.

It’s the “Write” Time to Exercise your Creative Writing Muscles

Just as our bodies need to be flexible and strong before we can choreograph dances, we need to strengthen our freedom of spirit, openness and courage to enjoy the process of creativity and the written word.

A new workshop–It's Always the Write Time–is a day of creative writing with renowned creative instructor Mimi Chenfeld. Writers of all levels and genres are invited. Register for one of two sessions: Saturday, April 24, 10 a.m.-2 p.m. (cost: $20) and Saturday, May 22, 9:30 a.m.-3:30 p.m. (cost: $30). Register online.

A Unique Way to Honor Who and What is Important to You

Park benches provide park-goers a place to take in the sights, have a rest or enjoy a conversation. We have more than 1,300 benches across more than 400 parks.

Did you know you can donate a park bench? It’s a wonderful way to memorialize a loved one, honor a cause or highlight the park you love. And it’s a great way to give back to your community. 

If you’re interested in donating a park bench in honor of a person or a cause that’s important to you, email Anna Defendiefer at ALDefendiefer@columbus.gov for more information and to discuss a location for the park bench.

Plan to Improve Aquatics Facilities Kick Off, Projects Moving Forward

Some Columbus residents refer to spring as “construction season” due to the increase in road improvement projects, and it’s no different here at Columbus Recreation and Parks! While the department works on improving parks, trails and facilities all year, there’s a lot of activity this spring.

Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan

One new project is the Aquatics Capital Improvement Plan. Many of Columbus Recreation and Parks Department’s aquatic facilities need or will soon need improvements to better serve residents. To make sure these facilities and the related programming meet the needs of residents, we are developing a long-term plan to invest in our aquatics programs and facilities over the coming years. One of the first steps is to see what you, our community, needs and wants to see. Your feedback will help shape the plan. Learn more about the project and how to share your feedback. 

Progress on many other projects continues. Highlights include:

  • A proposed design for the new Tuttle Park Skatepark is available for public comment: review the proposed design and share your feedback.

Double Your Impact: Donate to PLAY Today

The Brian S. Casey Family Memorial Fund is matching all gifts to PLAY Scholarship Fund this spring. The fund was established to honor Brian and his 19-year-old daughter, Megan, who tragically lost their lives in a plane crash in 2016. Brian was a strong believer in the PLAY program and served on the PLAY Golf Committee for many years. His wife, Sharon, started the fund to continue Brian’s commitment to the PLAY program.

Thanks to the generosity of the Casey Family, every dollar donated to the PLAY program this spring will be matched (up to $10,000). Please double your impact by making a donation today.

item.title: Celebrate Earth Month, Sign Up for Kickball and Celebrate with your Loved Ones
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

It’s Earth Month! Let’s Celebrate and Conserve

While we celebrate nature every month at Columbus Recreation and Parks Department, we’re always excited for Earth Month every April! It’s a great time to celebrate the connection that we have to nature and how it improves our physical and mental well-being. It’s also time to focus on how we can preserve and protect our environment.

Join us this April in celebrating Earth Month! Here are some things you can do:

Explore what’s waking up: As the weather warms, animals are venturing out, and plants are poking out of the ground. Check out what’s emerging in your backyard, neighborhood or park. Download the free iNaturalist app to identify your finds. Check back over the next few months to see how the habitat changes.

Do some spring cleaning: Clean up any litter that has accumulated over the winter. Practice safety measures such as wearing gloves. If you’re looking for an organized opportunity for your family or group, check out our volunteer program – volunteer opportunities are available throughout the year and include park cleanup events and invasive species removal.

Enjoy nature and get outside: Spending time outside is a great way to celebrate Earth Month, especially after being cooped up all winter! The fresh air and sunshine, combined with some physical activity, can boost your mood and help you stay fit. Take a walk on a trail or spend time in a park.

Plan a friendly garden: As plan your garden, consider planting a pollinator garden using native plants that bloom in the spring and fall. Native plants add to our local biodiversity and supports our wildlife. Consider planting milkweed, as they are the only plants that monarch caterpillars can eat. Limit pesticide use in your yard or garden. Franklin Soil and Water Conservation District's annual spring tree and plant sale features native plants – you can purchase plants anywhere. You can learn more about oaks, bees, wasps and other beneficial garden bugs by attending this free webinar series offered by OSU’s College of Food, Agricultural and Environmental Sciences.

New Leagues Respond to Kickball’s Growing Popularity

Kickball has gained in popularity in recent years. If you’re searching for a structured way to play the sport, look no further than CRPD Sports! You can join one or all of three seasons – spring, summer and fall. This is the second year for the leagues.

NEW! For the first time for any sport, you can sign up without a team. This new “free agent” registration allows anyone to play, even if you don’t have a full team.

The spring season starts April 11, with registration opening March 19. Learn more.  

Helping Artists Break In to the Professional Space

Know an emerging artist who’s looking for a start? Check out the Cultural Arts Center’s Loft Gallery! The Loft Gallery features smaller exhibitions, usually featuring the work of one or two artists. The program provides opportunities for artists to show their work in a great space, helps artists learn about the exhibition process, gives new artists gain first-time exposure and attracts and inspires visitors. It’s a great opportunity for up-and-coming artists, particularly those who have honed their skills in our classes!

Interested in having your artwork displayed? Learn how to submit your proposal.

Helping You Celebrate with Loved Ones

The public health emergency has reinforced the importance of connecting with family and friends. If you’re looking for a place to celebrate life’s most important events, the department’s rental venues reopened March 1 for events throughout 2021 and beyond. With a range of facilities including elegant wedding sites, shelterhouses with full kitchens and sites with fun playgrounds just steps away, there’s a facility that fits your group and your budget. Learn more about the different venues, and book your event.

We’re working to help keep you and your guests safe. All rental venues are cleaned between groups, and guests are required to follow health and safety guidelines.

Improving Facilities and Planning for the Future

As a resident of Columbus, the department manages more than 450 assets, which include community centers, parks, trails and pools, many of which are decades old. We are continually improving these facilities to ensure they meet the changing needs of residents, and to plan for future growth–Columbus is expected to grow by nearly 1 million residents by 2050!

As we work on these projects, it’s important that we get input from you, Columbus residents. That helps ensure improvements best meet the community’s needs. Watch this newsletter, our website and our Facebook, Twitter and Instagram accounts for information about upcoming projects. Currently, we’re asking for input for the Urban Forestry Master Plan, our strategic plan to invest in and improve the City’s trees.

Become a Champion for PLAY

Sometimes money is a barrier to helping kids engage in recreational opportunities. Studies show about 25 percent of kids report they don’t play sports often because it’s too expensive. And this number is expected to grow due to the impact of the coronavirus. Sports and other recreational opportunities are critical to kids’ mental and physical health.

The PLAY Scholarship Fund ensures kids can access fee-based programs like sports. You can support the fund by sponsoring or participating in the Champions for PLAY Golf Outing on May 7 at Champions Golf Course. Learn more.

item.title: Columbus Recreation and Parks - January News and Events
item.description:
Outdoor Winter Fun

There is plenty to see and do outdoors, no matter the season!

Getting outdoors in the winter is good for your mental and physical health. You’ll get some physical activity while soaking up some extra vitamin D, something that’s challenging during gray Ohio winters! The natural light, physical activity and mental engagement can lift your mood and energy levels.

Here are some fun ways to get outside this winter:

Take a winter hike: Take a hike on one of Columbus’ trails. With nearly 220 miles of trail, there’s a lot to explore!

Explore nature: Check out what lives and grows in the winter by exploring the great outdoors. Download the free iNaturalist app to help identify your finds. Add some fun by creating a scavenger hunt for your family, or host a virtual event with a larger group to engage with others in a safe way!

Visit a park: Go for a walk, host a winter picnic or enjoy the many amenities at your local park. Check out a list of our parks online. With nearly 400 parks, chances are you’ll find one around the corner that’s new to you!

Sign up for a guided activity: Looking for something more structured? Sign up for a variety of outdoor activities, including guided hikes and park clean up events, with our Outdoor Recreation team. Our safety protocols will ensure you’ll have fun and meet new people in a safe environment!

It’s important to stay safe outside! Be sure to dress for the weather – dress in layers made of wool or synthetic fabrics, and keep your head, hands and feet warm. Check out these tips from our partner REI for more information. Also, follow health and safety guidelines – practice social distancing, clean your hands often with soap and water or hand sanitizer and stay home if you’re not feeling well.

Keep Your Kids Engaged with Creative Activities

Staying home to keep warm and stay safe? Don’t let cabin fever set in! Keep engaged and get creative with our Art with Kids @ Home program. This video series offers a variety of easy, at-home art projects you can do with kids.

Check out the videos on YouTube – you can work through the projects on the schedule and pace that works best for your family. Share your creations on social media! Tag the department and use the hashtag #ArtWithKidsAtHome.

Free Produce Markets Resume in February

Access to fresh, nutritious food is critical to health. Many families in our community are struggling to purchase food and other basic necessities. To help residents, Columbus Recreation and Parks’ free Mobile Produce Markets will resume at select community centers in February. In 2020, markets provided nearly 305,000 meals to more than 25,000 residents.

Eligible families can receive a one-week supply of fresh produced, based on the family size. The drive-thru Mobile Produce Markets are staffed by volunteers wearing masks and gloves who load the produce directly into your trunk or car. Markets are first-come, first-served and last until produce runs out.

The first free Mobile Produce Market is Feb. 4, 3 p.m. at Glenwood Community Center, 1888 Fairmont Ave., 43223.

View an updated schedule online. Follow the department on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter and follow Go, Lunch! on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter for the most up to date information.

City Council Continues to Seek Community Input on Reimagining Safety Initiative

Columbus City Council invites residents to participate in a community survey designed to gain further insight on how to establish alternative crisis response models, invest in accountability and a better Division of Police, and invest in violence prevention. 

The 16-question survey asks users for their insights into safety in Columbus and how they want to see Council advance a budget that keeps all neighborhoods safe. Access the survey online, or copy and paste the link below in your browser:  

 www.surveymonkey.com/r/ReimagineSafety

The survey is another step in Council’s commitment to reimagining public safety driven by the people. In partnership with the Saunders PR Group, residents will participate in virtual town halls, focus group discussions and hearings. The information will be quantified to inform a comprehensive safety strategy that reinvests in neighborhoods, realigns safety protocols to specific community needs while creating a more equitable Columbus.

Read more about the Columbus City Council Reimagining Safety Initiative. 

Host Your Big Day with Us

Did you get engaged this holiday season? Columbus Recreation and Parks offers a variety of wedding venues that are perfect for your big day!

We offer many indoor and outdoor venues, including shelterhouses, open air shelters and premier event venues. Learn more about the many options, including the new The Gallery at Champions. Check out the Gallery's amenities on Wedding Wire and The Knot.

Did you know several Columbus Recreation and Parks' venues were nominated for the 2021 Best of Columbus Weddings? North Bank Park Pavilion, Park of Roses and the Cultural Arts Center were nominated in this annual readers’ poll that recognizes the top vendors in dozens of wedding-related categories.

Welcome to Our New Commission Members

Columbus Recreation and Parks is excited to welcome three new commissioners, Gregg Dodd, Letha Pugh and Jamie Wilson. Each community leader was appointed by Mayor Andrew J. Ginther and approved by Columbus City Council.

The Commission, appointed and organized under the Charter of the City of Columbus, provides leadership for the Department. The group includes a cross-functional team of leaders, who leverage their diversity and commitment to social equity to guide the Department in meeting the recreational needs of residents.  

Meet the new Commissioners and learn more about this important leadership group.

item.description:
Winter Registration Opens Jan. 4

Winter session registration begins Monday, Jan. 4. You can sign up for Active Learning Sites, which offer time blocks for independent school study and homework
assistance. Students can bring their computer–or
access a computer if needed–to complete and get
assistance with schoolwork. The winter session begins Jan. 11. Search and register for activities via Activenet, our online registration system. 

Strong safety protocols will still be in place to ensure the safety of all residents and staff. Advance registration is required for all activities, and everyone is required to wear face coverings and practice social distancing. 

Parks and trails continue to serve as a safe and accessible way to get outdoors. Although the weather is getting chilly, it is important to follow all safety protocols – practice social distancing, clean your hands often with soap and water or hand sanitizer and stay home if you’re not feeling well.

Carriage Place Players’ New Take on a Classic

Join Columbus Recreation and Park Department’s Carriage Place Players for A Christmas Carol: A Humbug On A String. This zany feature reimagines a holiday classic into a fun puppet show.

With in-person performances paused due to the public health emergency, the theater troupe created this virtual performance to bring some holiday spirit into residents' homes. You can watch the performance on Facebook and YouTube.

Start 2021 in a Healthy Way with Fitness Resolution Solution

We’re all looking for a fresh start in 2021!

Get your fitness goals off to a great start with our annual Fitness Resolution Solution program. This year, we’re hosting the event virtually Jan. 5-7. Join us each day at 10 a.m. and 6:30 p.m. for a variety of free classes designed for people of all ages, fitness levels and interests, including cardio fit, line dancing, abs, yoga, boxing and more.

Visit the Fitness Resolution Solution webpage and Facebook for more details. Registration is free and prizes/giveaways will be available to those who register and participate throughout the three-day event.

Recruit your family, friends and anyone who wants to get active and join us Jan. 5-7!

The Scioto Mile Lights Up for the Holidays 

Looking to enjoy some beautiful outdoor lights during the holiday season? Check out the Scioto Mile holiday lights! It's a great way to get some fresh air and exercise while getting in the holiday spirit. This free display is visible every day from dusk until dawn now through Jan. 3. 

View the lights safely–practice social distancing, clean your hands often with soap and water or hand sanitizer and stay home if you’re not feeling well.

Adopt A Center Makes the Holidays Brighter for Families

The pandemic has placed additional challenges and stressors on everyone, but vulnerable populations have been hit the hardest. The Adopt A Center program made it possible to remove some stress and help families enjoy the holiday season by providing more than 3,000 hot holiday meals, winter gear, toys and other needed supplies.

Individuals, organizations and companies made the program possible by purchasing gifts from the Columbus Recreation and Parks Department’s wish list, and donating toys, basic needs and monetary gifts. Every donation made a difference.

Thank you to our leading partners who made the program possible through financial and in-kind donations! 

Angel Partners: American Electric Power Foundation, Columbus Blue Jackets Foundation / Delta Dental

Celebration Partner: Mid-Ohio Food Collective

Festive Partners: Boar’s Head, AmeriHealth Caritas Ohio, Harmony Project

Holiday Partners: Crane Group, Easton Town Center, Lowe’s, Corrupted Public Records, Inc.

Jolly Partners: T & M Associates, Brown and Caldwell, T-Mobile, Humana Inc., Columbus Futsal Club, The Robert Weiler Company, MarshWagner, Seeds of Caring, Rogue Fitness
  • Dec. 25: Closed for Christmas Day
  • Jan. 1: Closed for New Year’s Day
  • Jan. 4: Winter Programming registration opens
  • Jan 5-7: Fitness Resolution Solution
  • Jan 7: Conversations and Coffee
  • Jan. 18: Closed for Martin Luther King Jr. Day

item.title: Columbus Recreation and Parks - November News and Events
item.description:
Department Wins Honors from OPRA

Columbus Recreation and Parks received a first place award in the Ohio Parks and Recreation Association (OPRA) Annual Awards of Excellence Program. OPRA supports parks and recreation professionals and organizations across Ohio in their efforts to provide quality facilities and recreational opportunities for all Ohioans while protecting and preserving Ohio’s natural resources. 

The award recognized the department’s efforts to address food insecurity through the Go, Lunch! free meal program and free mobile produce markets, and its efforts to connect residents with basic supplies and social services organizations with drive-through events and door-to-door canvassing. These efforts were added or adjusted to address the unique issues brought about by the pandemic. Read more about the awards program.

Receiving honors such as this underscores the department’s leadership in the industry and its commitment to improving the well-being of all residents.

Keeping Kids Active and Engaged

Columbus Recreation and Parks continues to offer programming for kids who are learning remotely, including hosting activities during the holiday break at the end of the year.

Active Learning Sites: Our 29 community centers are offering time blocks for independent school study and homework assistance. Students can bring their computer – or access a computer if needed – to complete and get assistance with schoolwork. Each community center follows the same scheduled Monday through Friday 9:30 a.m.–3 p.m. There is no cost to families. All participants must register in advance.

School’s Out: We will have activities during Winter Holiday Break 2020 for youth ages 6–12 years old. Winter break programming runs Monday, Dec. 21 through Thursday, Dec. 31 (closed Dec. 25 and Jan. 1 for the holidays). Online registration opens Monday, Dec. 7. All participants must register in advance.

The health and safety of participants and staff is our top priority. We have implemented rigorous, department-wide procedures, including daily wellness checks, a face covering requirement and social distancing protocols. Read more about these protocols.

Ulry/Warner Road Park Project Kicks Off

Do you live or work on the northeast side of Columbus? The department is asking for public input to help shape plans for a new 53-acre park at Ulry and Warner Roads.

Residents were invited to a virtual open house Nov. 10 to learn more about the project and to provide input on what would benefit their community. Residents can continue to provide input through Dec. 9 through this online survey.

Learn more about the project and share your thoughts.

City's Longest-running Artist Talks Return Virtually

The City’s longest-running series of artist talks, Conversations & Coffee, returned in a virtual format last month. Join us from the comfort of your home or office and gain key insight on art from a variety of people from different corners of the art world. Upcoming sessions include:

“D I S T A N C E” with Nicole Garlando: Loft Gallery artist Nicole “Cole” Garlando joins us at 12 p.m. on Thursday, Nov. 19 to discuss her work “D I S T A N C E” and share more of her studio practice. Join the conversation via Zoom.

“Essence of Character” with Kristin Morris: One of three current Main Gallery artists, Kristin Morris, joins us at 12 p.m. on Thursday, Dec. 3 to discuss the group exhibition “Essence of Character,” as well as individual studio practices and other upcoming projects in the works. Visit the CAC website for the link to join the Zoom meeting.

The Cultural Arts Center staff is excited to offer these lunchtime sessions after a brief hiatus due to the pandemic. Visit the CAC website for the current schedule.

Celebrate Green Friday and #OptOutside

Turn Black Friday green this year–get outside and enjoy the day!

Our friends at REI encourage everyone to #OptOutside and enjoy fresh air and family - make Nov. 27 Green Friday. Not only will you avoid the crowds, you’ll benefit from the fresh air and physical activity!

This year, Columbus Recreation and Parks is joining parks and recreation departments from across the country in a Green Friday campaign. Join the Facebook event to get ideas about things to see and do. Share your adventures on social media–use the hashtag #OptOutside and tag Columbus Recreation and Parks Department to share how you celebrate Green Friday!

Local Companies Give Back: You Can, Too!

The Adopt a Center program offers many ways to help families in need this holiday season. Whether you are a large company, a small organization or an individual, you can help!

Columbus Futsal Club has made a financial donation to the Adopt a Center effort and encouraged its members to support the effort by purchasing toys. T&M Associates, an engineering firm, has adopted a center and is encouraging other local engineering firms to join their efforts.

And many individuals have already gone to the Amazon Wish List and purchased a gift or two for a child in need.

This year has been a difficult one. Many low income adults have lost their job, resulting in families struggling to pay for basic needs. Please consider helping us to bring some holiday joy to these families. Learn how you can make a difference.
  • Nov. 19: Conversations and Coffee
  • Nov. 26: Thanksgiving Day–Facilities Closed
  • Nov. 27: Green Friday #OptOutside
  • Dec. 3: Conversations and Coffee
  • Dec. 9: Ulry/Warner Park–Public Comments Close
  • Dec. 25: Christmas Day–Facilities Closed

item.title: Columbus Recreation and Parks News and Events
item.description:
Welcome to your Columbus Recreation and Parks Department!

Columbus Recreation and Parks Department offers many ways for residents of all ages to connect with nature, wellness and creativity. There’s programming that appeals to every interest and age, whether it’s preschool programming, open swim time, access to a Get Active fitness center or water aerobics. This monthly newsletter will connect you with what’s coming up so you can take advantage of all your Columbus Recreation and Parks Department has to offer!

Know someone else who would like to receive this information? Sign up here.

Fall Program Registration Opens Oct. 26

Registration for the second session of fall programming begins Oct. 26. This fall, a significant number of programs, classes and facilities resumed, reaching residents of all ages. Highlights include Learning Activity blocks that offer students structured opportunities to focus on schoolwork; educational and physical activity programs; fitness rooms and fitness classes; open swim and lap swim; and senior arts programming. Read more about fall programming and how to register.

Your health and safety is our priority. You will see new safety protocols and adjusted formats, including limited group sizes, advanced registration for all programs and facilities and required face coverings. Read more about safety protocols.

Improving Our Trails: Fifth to Griggs Biking and Walking Study

Columbus’ parks and trails add to the quality of life in our community. Columbus Recreation and Parks continually invests in facilities to ensure residents have access to these vital resources.

The Scioto Trail currently ends at West Fifth Avenue (view a map of the Scioto Trail). Plans for future trail construction leave a gap in the regional trail network between West Fifth Avenue and Griggs Park. Columbus Recreation and Parks is exploring ways to address the gap and improve walking and biking facilities in the study area. Learn more about the project.

Maintaining and Enhancing our Urban Forest

Columbus’ urban forest, or all trees on public and private property throughout the city, is critical to our quality of life. Trees improve mental and physical health, reduce air and water pollution, alleviate heat stress, make streets safer and more walkable, increase wildlife habitat and lead to higher property values.

Columbus is developing its first-ever Urban Forestry Master Plan to map out a long-term strategy to maintain and enhance Columbus’ urban forest. Learn more, including how you can help shape the plan.

Creating Spaces for Connection 

Core to Columbus Recreation and Parks' mission is connecting our community. You can celebrate while enjoying one of the beautiful parks that our great City has to offer! Whether you're hosting a baby shower, retirement party, wedding or business meeting, there's a facility for every event and budget.

Planning a wedding, corporate event or golf outing in 2021? Check out The Gallery at Champions at the Champions Golf Course, a brand-new venue located only 10 minutes from Easton. Learn more about Champions and all rental spaces.

Make a Difference this Holiday Season

Columbus Recreation and Parks serves seniors, adults, children and people with disabilities across 31 community centers and programs throughout Columbus. More importantly, these centers serve as a connection point for resources focused on helping those in need.

This holiday season, Columbus Recreation and Parks will provide meals, hygiene items, winter coats and clothing for families as well as holiday toys for kids. We are looking for groups, organizations, businesses and individuals to help support our efforts through the Adopt a Center program. Learn more about how you can make a difference this holiday season.

  • Oct. 26: Community Recreation Session 2 registration opens

  • Nov. 14-15: Turkey Bowl Softball Tournament; registration opens Oct. 23
